# dsh-link-actions
English | 中文
Right-click menus for links in DeepSeek Harness chat. File and folder links gain **open**, **open wi
th**, **show in file manager**, **copy path**, and **save as**; HTTP(S) links gain **open in browser
** and **copy link**.
## Why a plugin
The DSH repository does not accept external pull requests today, and the plugin ecosystem is the pat
h it recommends instead. The client also has no per-link slot: a Markdown link is a plain anchor or
button, so this plugin listens for `contextmenu` on the document, recognises the two link shapes the
Markdown renderer emits, and draws its own menu.
Tested against the shipped `0.2.1-rc.2` runtime. It needs a DSH client build that serves client plug
ins; the desktop app and `dsh web` both do.

## Menu
File and folder links — the filename buttons and `fileMention` chips in a message:
| Item | Behavior |
| Open | Hand the path to the Host desktop's default application; a folder opens in the file manager

|
| Open with › | List the registered handlers for the file and open it with one |
| Show in file m

anager | Reveal the file with it selected |
| Copy path | Copy the resolved absolute path |
| Save a
s… | Read the file's bytes and write them to a location you pick |
HTTP(S) links — ordinary `<a>` elements in the message:
| Item | Behavior |

| Open in browser | Open the URL in a new window |
| Copy link | Copy the href |
## How it works
- **Where the path comes from.** The renderer puts the full path in a file link's `title` (the resol
ver supplies it for `fileMention`, the authored destination for `MarkdownFileLink`); when there is n

o `title`, the button text is the path.
- **Relative paths.** They are joined with the viewing Sessi

on's `cwd`. The Host resolves relative paths against its own process cwd, which would be wrong.
- **
Existing Remotes only.** `session.canOpenWorkspacePath`, `session.workspacePathApplications`, `sessi

on.openWorkspacePath`, and `workspaceFiles.readBytes`; the plugin ships no transport of its own.
- *
*Product design tokens.** `--dsw-menu-surface-fill`, `--dsw-elevation-prominent`, `--dsw-alias-*`, s

o the card follows the active theme.
- **No runtime dependencies.** The client half is one self-cont
ained ES2022 script; the build only wraps it in the DSH module-loader handshake (`window.__ModuleLoa
der__.load({ id, factory })`). No bundler.
## Verified
Against the shipped `0.2.1-rc.2` runtime, with the same client bundle that npm serves:
| Scenario | Result |
| Install from npm | `dsh plugin add dsh-link-actions` (0.1.0, 8 files / 71.5 kB), fresh profile, cl

ient boot, menu opens |
| Install from GitHub | `dsh plugin add github:InnovationLou/dsh-link-action

s`, fresh profile, client boot, menu opens |
| Right-click a folder link | Five items: open, open wi

th, show in file manager, copy path, save as |
| "Open with" on an image | Real handlers listed: Pai

nt, Photos, VS Code, Typora, Notepad++, … |
| "Save as" on a png | "Saved" notice, file landed in th

e download directory under its own name |
| Right-click an HTTP(S) link | Two items: open in browser

, copy link |
| Relative path | `ai-niang-images\fish-01-classic.png` resolved through the Session c

py link |
| Relative path | `ai-niang-images\fish-01-classic.png` resolved through the Session cwd |
Open and Show in file manager go through the same `session.openWorkspacePath` call (the `reveal` bra
nch was checked in code) but were not exercised by automation against real windows.
## Limitations
- **Transcript only.** Links outside `[data-chat-flow]` — the sidebar, the document preview — keep t

heir native behavior.
- **No "open with" for folders.** The OS has no folder-level associations, so

that item removes itself when the list resolves empty.
- **`label` links.** The button carries only

the label the author wrote; when no real path can be recovered, only Copy path is offered.
- **Save
as is bounded** by the Host's `workspaceFiles` read limit (`maxFileBytes`); a directory cannot be sa

ved this way.
- **Application icons may not render.** They come from the Host's `open-in-app/icon/<i

d>` route; a missing icon removes its slot so the labels stay aligned.
- **Internal surfaces.** The
`dsh.client` declaration, the Remote names, `data-chat-flow`, and the `fileMention`/`fileLink` CSS-m
odule classes are product internals; re-check after a DSH upgrade.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`tools/` holds the local verification helpers (Node 24 ships `WebSocket`, so they talk to CDP direct
ly): `cdp-contextmenu.mjs` for the link menu, `cdp-file-menu.mjs` for the file menu, `cdp-open-with.
mjs` for the submenu, `cdp-save-as.mjs` for an end-to-end save, `cdp-screenshot.mjs` for a capture,
and `asar-head.mjs` to read the installed `app.asar`.
`test/overlay.yml` mounts the plugin into a throwaway CLI profile:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
so verification never touches the profile you use daily.
## Releasing

Publishing runs on npm **Trusted Publishing**: the `release` workflow asks GitHub
for an OIDC token,

npm exchanges it for a short-lived publish grant, and no npm
token is stored in the repository or i

n any secret. That keeps the account's
"require 2FA and disallow bypass tokens" setting intact — the

re is no token that
could bypass it.

One-time setup, on npmjs.com → the package → **Settings → Trusted Publisher
